title: bug records written by bug-add validate against the published schema
desiredOutcome: A plan whose bugs were filed by bug-add with no repro, expected or actual validates under the published schema (ajv draft2020, CI's manifest validation job) as it does under validate-manifest, and validate-manifest reports every bug value the schema rejects - a warning inside the 3.x line that names 4.0.0 as the release that refuses it, per COMPATIBILITY's additive-validation promise - so the two validators can no longer disagree silently on bug records

findings.issue: The phase's desiredOutcome promises that validate-manifest rejects a bug field the schema rejects; _check_bugs checks required fields, unknown keys, the id pattern, the status enum, ado and the taskId link but no value type, so a bug with repro 7, files as a string, severity 3 or description null passes validate-manifest and fails CI's ajv step - the two validators still disagree on any record the verb did not write.
findings.resolution: Type each bug value against the schema's bug item, derived from the schema file rather than a second table; a case walks the schema's bug properties and shows validate-manifest refuses a wrong-typed value for each, with the allow twin of each admitted type.

findings.issue: The in-test reader counts a node as a fault only when it understands none of its keywords, so a node with one understood and one unread keyword (the id's type+pattern) is admitted on the understood part, and keywords beside $ref are dropped.
findings.resolution: Return 'cannot read' for any constraint keyword outside the read set (annotations excepted), read pattern, merge $ref siblings; a row with a pattern-violating id must be reported.

findings.issue: Only the no-flag bug-add record is typed against the schema; the record written with every optional flag is not.
The entry says every key is spelled like its nullable neighbours and that every key the verb writes is held, but repro gains a oneOf null arm and only the no-flag record is held.
findings.resolution: Say what was done for each key and which record is held.

findings.issue: validate() is documented as pure - it reads no file and holds no module state, which is why the panel, audit-task's pre- and post-write checks and migrate-manifest share it - while _check_bugs now reads the schema from disk on every call for a plan holding bugs, and an unreadable schema becomes a finding inside that pure function.
findings.resolution: Pass the schema in as a second injected input, like today=: validate(manifest, today=None, schema=None) threads it to _check_bugs; the entry points load it once per process and hand it in; the docstring names the schema as the second input and says when a fallback read happens.

findings.issue: The dedupe is keyed by top-level property, so one hand-written ado finding hides a different schema fault in the same object (ado {id 7, url 5, origin x} reports origin only), contradicting the CHANGELOG's every-present-value claim and COMPATIBILITY's reported-once sentence.
findings.resolution: Record the path each hand-written check refused and drop only schema reasons at or under that path; a case for the ado example must give the origin finding and one ado.url warning.

findings.issue: Patterns run through Python re.search, whose \d matches any Unicode digit and whose $ matches before a trailing newline, so 'BUG-1\n' and an id with a non-ASCII digit pass every local check and fail ajv (ECMA-262 with the u flag), contradicting COMPATIBILITY's sentence that the warning always names what the published schema says.
findings.resolution: Match with re.ASCII and translate an unescaped trailing $ to \Z before compiling, and give BUG_ID_RE the same treatment or refuse a trailing newline; both strings as refused samples in a case.

findings.issue: Enum membership requires equal JSON type names, so 1.0 is not in [1], while draft 2020-12 compares numbers by value; no reachable enum is numeric today, so it cannot fire yet and nothing at build time would catch it.
findings.resolution: Treat integer and number as one class for enum/const (booleans excluded); a case where 1.0 is in [1] and True is not.

findings.issue: The suffix says validate-manifest refuses such a value from 4.0.0 in the present tense and never says the plan still validates in 3.x, so a reader can take the warning for a failure.
findings.resolution: Say the published schema refuses the value, validate-manifest will refuse it from 4.0.0, and it is a warning in 3.x; update the pinned substrings.

findings.issue: The _validator docstring says an unreadable schema makes the verb's pre-check refuse rather than write, but signoff, group and seed have no pre-check: on a broken install they write, fail the post-write validation, roll back and blame the user's change ('would leave the manifest invalid').
findings.resolution: Carry the unreadable findings on the validator and have signoff, group and seed refuse on them before writing, with the install-broken sentence; a case per verb.

review.outcome: [findings: 10 - 0 high, 2 med, 8 low; 0 with a recorded fix commit]

tasks.title: the schema admits null for a bug's repro, expected and actual, as it does for its neighbours
tasks.description: bug-add writes the documented shape (bug.md: every key present, an absent answer as null); the schema admits null for reportedBy, taskId, fixedIn and notes but not repro, expected, actual, so CI's ajv step rejects every plan with a bug-add record lacking them while validate-manifest (which does not apply the schema) accepts it. Admit null there (COMPATIBILITY: adding is free), and pin that the record bug-add writes with no optional flag carries only values the schema's declared type for each key admits

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: a bug written by bug-add with no --repro/--expected/--actual carries, for every key, a value the schema's declared type for that bug key admits
